title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Parts of Speech - Adverbs
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the adverb of frequency in the following sentence:
"She rarely arrives late for her morning classes."
questions.explain: Adverbs of frequency describe how often an action occurs. 'Rarely' tells us the frequency of her arriving late, meaning it does not happen often.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct adverbial structure:
"Hardly _____ the house when the thunderstorm began."
questions.explain: When a sentence begins with a negative adverb like 'Hardly', 'Scarcely', or 'Rarely', it triggers subject-auxiliary inversion. Therefore, 'had he left' is the correct structure.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct intensifier for the sentence:
"It was _____ bad weather that we decided to stay indoors all day."
questions.explain: Because 'weather' is an uncountable noun, we use 'such' before the adjective-noun phrase, not 'such a'. 'So' is typically followed by an adjective without a noun.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct adverb of manner:
"The student answered the headmaster's question _____."
questions.explain: An adverb of manner modifies how an action is performed. 'Politely' modifies the verb 'answered' to show how the student responded.
questions.subject: English Studies
